page.title: Compare
page.purpose: Elicit preference efficiently by asking which of two candidates is preferred, and show the listener that their effort is moving the model.

priorities.statement: Declining to choose is always available; a forced choice produces a false label.
The listener can hear enough of each candidate to judge before being asked to decide.
Effort is visibly rewarded — the listener can see that comparisons are reducing the model's uncertainty.

states.description: Two full tracks presented for comparison.
Two isolated elements presented for comparison.
Not enough analysed material to form an informative pair.

elements.description: First candidate with its own playback control.
Second candidate with its own playback control.
Decline to choose between the candidates.

claims.statement: A no-preference option is present whenever a comparison is offered.
Both candidates expose independent playback before a judgement is requested.
The listener is told whether they are comparing whole tracks or isolated elements.
The effect of accumulated comparisons on model uncertainty is visible.
The two candidates are presented at equal visual weight so position does not bias the judgement.
